messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression in per-token TTFT on canary today. p50 looks fine but p95/p99 have a fat microtail. traces show a bunch of tokens hitting a "fallthrough" in the kernel selector after a KV prefetch miss.

aj: do you have a snippet of the trace or selector logs?

maria: pasted a short trace (sanitized) below:
```
selector.choose kernel_variant=fast_cuda
prefetch.kv lookup=miss
kernel_launch(cpu_fallback) start
kernel_launch(cpu_fallback) end dt=8200us
postprocess dt=120us
```

samir: ugh — cpu_fallback tokens explain the big tail. we need token-granular attribution not just per-request spans. current tracing collapses multiple tokens into one big decode span.

karen: Agreed. proposal: add an atomic token-level span around the kernel selection + kernel execution, with tags: kernel_variant, kv_prefetch_hit (true/false), fallback_reason (if any), route, model, seq_len_bucket. Sample at 0.5% default. Also emit per-token micro-histo (us) to a hot path metric.

oliver: how do we keep overhead acceptable? full otel spans per token will kill throughput. maybe inline counters + ring buffer that we flush async. e.g., per-worker circular buffer of (kernel_id, dt_us, prefetch_hit) entries and a background thread aggregates to histograms. cheap and low-allocation.

samir: exactly. two-tier approach: cheap inlined samples for aggregate histograms + occasional full otel span for sampled tokens so we can reassemble token-level waterfall. the inlined path should be ~100-300ns per token (memstore + counter), full span ~10-30us and sampled at <1%.

maria: dashboard UX idea: per-route token waterfall split into prequeue, selector, prefetch, kernel_launch, decode, postprocess. show p50/p95/p99 and token counts. clicking a point expands sampled token traces.

aj: metrics we need: counter kvcache.prefetch_hit{route,model}, counter kernel.fallback{reason}, histogram token.kernel_latency_us{kernel_variant,route,model,seq_bucket}. also a gauge for ring-buffer lag.

karen: add fallback_reason values = [no_kernel_match, kv_miss, memory_pressure, quant_fallback]. please include that in the selector logs and in the tag.

maria: operational note — for experiments, enable higher sample rate only on canaries (route tag = canary) and for routes with recent regressions. keeps prod overhead minimal.

oliver: short prototype sketch (pseudocode):
```c
// hot path
entry = ringbuf[atomic_inc(&write_idx) % N];
entry->kernel_id = kernel_id;
entry->dt_us = dt_us;
entry->prefetch = prefetch_hit;
// background flusher aggregates to histograms every 500ms
```

samir: action items:
1) runtime change: inlined ring-buffer + kvcache.prefetch_hit counter (samir)
2) selector: emit fallback_reason tag (maria)
3) tracing: sampled full token spans (karen)
4) console: token waterfall panel & toggle to show sampled traces (aj)
5) perf: run canary workload (100k tokens) and compare p95/p99 before/after (oliver)

samir: I'll open a design PR with perf numbers and a small benchmark harness. estimate 2 weeks for prototype + 1 week for dashboard wiring.

maria: TY — please add expected overhead numbers and the flush cadence to the PR.

maria: @deploy-bot can we schedule a canary run with the prototype after the first PR lands? :eyes:

deploy-bot: scheduled canary job `canary/rt-token-instr-176600` for 2025-03-04T14:05:00Z. traces will land under /traces/1766001234-canary and metrics in the perf cluster. :white_check_mark:

karen: one more: add a boolean tag `kvcache.prefetch_tried` vs `prefetch_hit` so we can disambiguate routes that don't prefetch at all.

maria: good call. I'll add that to the checklist in the GH issue.

aj: leaving a quick note — we should also ensure telemetry keys are cardinality-safe (route/model low-cardinality buckets). use seq_len buckets like [<=32, 33-128, 129-512, 513+].

maria: done for now. ping me in the PR for review. :thumbsup:
